    indexer_decode_cp = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.indexer_decode_cp*
        Split the sparse-attention indexer's decode scoring across the
        tensor-parallel ranks by context instead of by index head: each
        rank scores a 1/TP slice of the index-K pages for every head and
        the ranks exchange their local top-k, so each reads 1/TP of the
        index-K cache per sparse layer. The index-K cache stays
        replicated, so this is unrelated to
        `--decode-context-parallel-size`, which shards the KV cache
        itself; the two cannot be combined. Implemented for the MiniMax
        M3 NVFP4 indexer, which needs `indexer_kv_dtype="nvfp4"` and TP
        4 (one index head per rank); it is ignored with a warning where
        it does not apply. It pays off from about 4 concurrent decodes
        at 128K context and grows with batch and context.

    indexer_kv_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.indexer_kv_dtype*
        Data type for the sparse-attention indexer K cache. "auto" picks
        the model's default (bf16 for MiniMax M3, fp8 for the DeepSeek
        sparse indexer, mxfp4 for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm CDNA4 with aiter).
        Quantized formats (fp8, mxfp4, nvfp4) require indexer kernel
        support in the backend; MiniMax M3 supports nvfp4 on
        SM100/SM103/SM107 with at most 8 decode queries per request.

    indexer_logits_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.indexer_logits_dtype*
        Output dtype of DeepGEMM's dense MQA-logits kernels in the
        DeepSeek sparse-attention indexer. "auto" (default) picks the
        model's default: "bfloat16" for DeepSeek-V3.2 and DeepSeek-V4 on
        SM100, "float32" otherwise. "float32" reduces the head-weighted
        scores in FP32 and feeds them to the top-k as is. "bfloat16"
        halves the logits memory; on SM100 it also reduces in BF16 with
        BF16 head weights and lets the DeepSelect top-k rank the logits
        directly, while other top-k kernels read an FP32 copy. The
        sparse MQA-logits path (`indexer_sparse_logits`) emits BF16 on
        SM100 and FP32 on SM90 and ROCm, independently of this setting.

    indexer_sparse_logits = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits*
        Score only candidate blocks in the DeepSeek V4.1 two-level
        indexer. None (default) enables it on SM90 and supported SM100
        configurations; True forces it; False uses dense scoring.
        Requires no context parallelism. SM90 uses CuTe DSL with FP8
        cache and dense fallback for short prefills. Unsupported cache,
        model geometry or microbatching raises at initialization,
        including with the default None. SM100 requires DeepGEMM >= 2.8
        and DeepSelect (FP8/MXFP4 cache). ROCm gfx950 uses aiter with
        MXFP4 cache and remains opt-in.

    minimax_m3_indexer_cp = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_indexer_cp*
        MiniMax M3 on ROCm with tensor_parallel_size > 1: score the
        sparse indexer context-parallel at decode. Each rank reads 1/TP
        of the index cache, scores every index head on it, and per-head
        top-k candidates are exchanged and merged, so the selected
        blocks match the default path. `indexer_kv_dtype` picks the
        kernels that do it: a bf16 index cache ("auto" or "bf16") runs
        the Triton CP indexer, an fp8 e4m3 one the AITER MSA CP indexer
        on gfx950. This shards indexer work and not the KV cache, so it
        is not `decode_context_parallel_size` and requires that to be 1.

    minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend = 'cutlass' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend*
        Sparse decode kernel used by the MiniMax M3 MSA backend.
        "cutlass" falls back to Triton where the CUTLASS kernel does not
        support the platform, KV cache dtype, or head layout.

    mla_prefill_backend = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.mla_prefill_backend*
        MLA prefill backend to use. If None, will be selected
        automatically. Valid options: FLASH_ATTN (FA3/FA4), FLASHINFER,
        TRTLLM_RAGGED; on ROCm, ROCM_AITER_FA and ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8.
        ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 is opt-in (gfx950, bf16 models): it
        quantizes Q/K/V to FP8 per tensor at runtime and falls back to
        ROCM_AITER_FA for inputs the FlyDSL kernel cannot take.

    sparse_mla_force_mqa = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_force_mqa*
        Force sparse MLA to use forward_mqa for all requests, including
        prefill. When False (default), pure prefill batches use
        forward_mha when implemented. Set to True to always use the MQA
        path.

    sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor = Field(default=None, ge=2)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor*
        Sparse MLA prefill workspace size, in multiples of
        `max_model_len`. FlashMLA sparse gathers a prefill step's
        context KV into this workspace and runs attention in more chunks
        when the step holds more. The sparse indexer's prefill K buffer
        is sized to fit in the same memory. Lower values return memory
        to the KV cache at long `max_model_len`; the minimum of 2 leaves
        room for a full-length request's context-parallel shard. If
        None, 5 when `max_model_len` is at most 256K tokens, else 2.

    sparse_mla_shard_q = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_shard_q*
        Under tensor parallelism, shard sparse-MLA (DSA) prefill by
        token instead of by head: each TP rank runs the indexer and the
        sparse attention for its slice of the tokens with all heads, and
        all-to-all exchanges move the query and the attention output
        between the layouts. Applies to steps with at least
        `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` prefill tokens on the FlashInfer
        sparse MLA backend, or on FlashMLA sparse with an FP8 DeepSeek
        KV cache, without DCP, PCP or HiSparse. A mixed step's decode
        tokens stay sharded by head.

    sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens = Field(default=1024, ge=1)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens*
        Minimum number of tokens after a step's decodes (requests of at
        most 1 + num_speculative_tokens tokens) for `sparse_mla_shard_q`
        to apply. Below it the all-to-all exchanges can cost more than
        they save.

    tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv = Field(default=1, ge=1, le=256)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.AttentionConfig.tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv*
        Minimum KV splits for TokenSpeed MLA decode. The default of 1
        preserves automatic scheduling. Larger values request a split
        floor and may increase workspace memory. Only applies to the
        TokenSpeed MLA backend.

    tq_max_kv_splits_for_cuda_graph = 32 class-attribute

    device_buffer_size = Field(default=None, gt=0) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.HiSparseConfig.device_buffer_size*
        Total per-request GPU hot-buffer rows, including the
        newest-token slot.

        Defaults to one top-k per decode query plus one top-k of LRU
        slack. The physical allocation is rounded up to the GPU cache
        block size selected from the active backends.

    eager_host_mirror = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.attention.HiSparseConfig.eager_host_mirror*
        Mirror decode-written KV rows to the host pool during the
        forward so page spills complete without moving data. When
        disabled, decode rows stay resident-only and evicted pages are
        copied to host at spill time. Prefill rows are always mirrored
        during the forward.

    cache_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.cache_dtype*
        Data type for kv cache storage. If "auto", will use model data
        type. An explicit float16 or bfloat16 must match the model data
        type. Custom dtypes can registered by platform backends via
        `register_kv_cache_dtype` are accepted (see vllm.config.cache).
        CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3) and fp8_e5m2. ROCm (AMD GPU)
        supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3). Intel Gaudi (HPU) supports fp8 (using
        fp8_inc). Some models (namely DeepSeekV3.2) default to fp8, set
        to bfloat16 to use bfloat16 instead, this is an invalid option
        for models that do not default to fp8. "nvfp4_4over6" uses the
        NVFP4 layout and selects between max/6 and max/4 scales per 16
        values by minimizing squared reconstruction error.

    enable_extensible_kv_cache = Field(default=None) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.enable_extensible_kv_cache*
        Reserve the KV cache address range with device virtual memory
        and commit physical pages after warmup, so the cache is sized
        from the memory actually free after CUDA graph capture rather
        than from a profiling estimate. If unspecified, enabled on CUDA
        and ROCm unless kv_cache_memory_bytes is set, or NIXL on device
        memory has no IMEX channel; falls back to estimate-based sizing
        where the driver lacks VMM support. Explicitly requesting it
        where unsupported is an error. On unpartitioned discrete ROCm
        GPUs, the sizing adds back free memory that HIP hides by
        counting each allocation as at least 2 MiB, so
        gpu_memory_utilization bounds exact device memory use there.
        When a KV connector registers the KV cache for RDMA or exports
        it to another process, each segment is backed by a single
        physical allocation; connectors declare this by overriding
        `KVConnectorBase_V1.kv_cache_access`.

    gpu_memory_utilization = Field(default=None, gt=0, le=1)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.gpu_memory_utilization*
        The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor,
        which can range from 0 to 1. For example, a value of 0.5 would
        imply 50% GPU memory utilization. This is a per-instance limit,
        and only applies to the current vLLM instance. It does not
        matter if you have another vLLM instance running on the same
        GPU. For example, if you have two vLLM instances running on the
        same GPU, you can set the GPU memory utilization to 0.5 for each
        instance. On non-GPU installs, this value controls the
        corresponding device memory utilization.

        If unspecified, 1.0 with the extensible KV cache (sized from
        measured memory) and 0.92 otherwise; see
        `resolved_gpu_memory_utilization`.

        With the extensible KV cache (the default on CUDA and ROCm),
        leave this unset unless something needs memory that vLLM does
        not measure: other processes sharing the GPU (including ones
        that allocate after vLLM has started), unified-memory devices
        whose memory the CPU also uses, weight transfer buffers for
        weight updates, or KV connectors that allocate their own device
        buffers. A lower value takes memory away from the KV cache.

    kv_cache_layout = field(default=None, init=False)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.kv_cache_layout*
        Resolved physical KV cache layout name (a `KVCacheLayout`
        member).

        `None` means the layout has not been resolved yet. The engine
        core resolves it once (`resolve_kv_cache_layout`) before memory
        profiling, and every worker process adopts the resolved name ---
        via the `set_kv_cache_layout` RPC, or
        `KVCacheConfig.kv_cache_layout` for workers spawned after
        resolution --- before the KV cache is allocated. Once set the
        value is final and read with `get_resolved_kv_cache_layout`,
        which raises on `None`. Tests and standalone tools may pre-set a
        value, which resolution then honors as-is.

    prefix_cache_retention_interval = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.prefix_cache_retention_interval*
        Token interval between retained sliding-window and Mamba
        prefix-cache checkpoints. `0` retains only semantic checkpoints,
        including the latest replay boundary and shared-prefix
        junctions. Positive values additionally retain periodic
        checkpoints at the specified interval, which must be a multiple
        of the scheduler block size. `None` retains checkpoints densely.
        Applies only to sliding-window and Mamba cache groups.

    prefix_caching_hash_algo = 'sha256' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.prefix_caching_hash_algo*
        Set the hash algorithm for prefix caching:

        - "sha256" uses Pickle for object serialization before hashing.
          This is the current default, as SHA256 is the most secure
          choice to avoid potential hash collisions.
        - "sha256_cbor" provides a reproducible, cross-language
          compatible hash. It serializes objects using canonical CBOR
          and hashes them with SHA-256.
        - "xxhash" uses Pickle serialization with xxHash (128-bit) for
          faster, non-cryptographic hashing. Requires the optional
          `xxhash` package. IMPORTANT: Use of a hashing algorithm that
          is not considered cryptographically secure theoretically
          increases the risk of hash collisions, which can cause
          undefined behavior or even leak private information in
          multi-tenant environments. Even if collisions are still very
          unlikely, it is important to consider your security risk
          tolerance against the performance benefits before turning this
          on.
        - "xxhash_cbor" combines canonical CBOR serialization with
          xxHash for reproducible hashing. Requires the optional
          `xxhash` package.

    prefix_match_unit = Field(default=None, gt=0) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.prefix_match_unit*
        The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can
        land on.

        Prefix-cache keys are computed every `prefix_match_unit` tokens.
        It can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g.
        32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache
        group's `block_size` is divisible by it, enabling cache hits at
        boundaries inside a physical block. It controls matching
        granularity only, not how often states are stored.

        This equals to the `hash_block_size` used throughout the KV
        cache code.

    replayssm_buffer_len = Field(default=16, gt=0) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.replayssm_buffer_len*
        ReplaySSM logical history length B for Mamba2. Triton standard
        decode uses B physical rows; FlashInfer and Triton speculative
        decoding use B+T, where T is the target verification length.
        Kimi-K3 speculative decode does not use B. Default 16.

    swa_bounded_replay = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay*
        Keep the sliding-window KV of models that support it
        (DeepSeek-V4.1) out of prefix caching and rebuild it after a
        prefix hit by recomputing the hit's last window. The layers past

    use_kda_recoverssm = field(default=False, init=False)

    use_replayssm = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.cache.CacheConfig.use_replayssm*
        Use the ReplaySSM Mamba2 decode kernel: cache recent SSM inputs
        and skip the per-step full-state store, writing the checkpoint
        back only on flush. Triton and FlashInfer support Mamba prefix
        caching on and off. Mamba2 speculative decoding supports both
        backends. Pipeline parallelism is not supported. Flushes are
        most efficient when mamba_block_size is a multiple of
        replayssm_buffer_len, but this is not required.

                                       *vllm.config.cache.KVCacheDTypeHandler*

KVCacheDTypeHandler
    Bases: `Protocol`

    Contract for a custom `--kv-cache-dtype` value.

    A platform backend implements this protocol to answer the questions
    vLLM currently answers with closed tables
    (`STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE` / `get_kv_quant_mode` /
    `is_quantized_kv_cache`). A single handler may be device-aware
    (e.g., resolving different torch dtypes per device generation).

    Methods: ~

    quant_mode   The `KVQuantMode` used by generic kernels.
    torch_dtype  Storage dtype for KV cache tensors.

    quant_mode()
    *vllm.config.cache.KVCacheDTypeHandler.quant_mode*
        The `KVQuantMode` used by generic kernels.

        Return an existing mode to reuse generic kernel paths, or
        `KVQuantMode.CUSTOM` when the backend fully self-manages kernel
        dispatch.

    torch_dtype()
    *vllm.config.cache.KVCacheDTypeHandler.torch_dtype*
        Storage dtype for KV cache tensors.

        Called once at registration time; the result is injected into
        the shared `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE` dict so existing consumers
        need no changes. The device must already be resolvable
        (registration runs at platform activation time).

                                *vllm.config.cache.get_kv_cache_dtype_handler*

get_kv_cache_dtype_handler(name)
    Return the handler for `name`.

    Returns None for upstream dtypes that have no handler (the dtype
    table already covers these).

                                   *vllm.config.cache.is_known_kv_cache_dtype*

is_known_kv_cache_dtype(name)

                                   *vllm.config.cache.register_kv_cache_dtype*

register_kv_cache_dtype(name)
    Register a custom `--kv-cache-dtype` value (eager decorator).

    Runs at platform activation time (first `current_platform` access),
    which is after `--help` exits and before any KV cache tensor is
    allocated. During decoration the handler will:

    - append `name` to the mutable `KV_CACHE_DTYPES` list (driving
      Pydantic + CLI validation);
    - resolve `torch_dtype()` once and inject it into
      `STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE`, so all existing `dict[name]` /
      `name in dict` sites need zero changes;
    - be stored for later `quant_mode()` queries.

    Examples: ~

    >python
        >>> @register_kv_cache_dtype("int8")
        ... class Int8Handler:
        ...     name = "int8"
        ...
        ...     def torch_dtype(self):
        ...         return torch.int8
        ...
        ...     def quant_mode(self):
        ...         return KVQuantMode.CUSTOM

CUDAGraphMode

                                   *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig*

CompilationConfig
    Configuration for compilation.

    You must pass CompilationConfig to VLLMConfig constructor.
    VLLMConfig's post_init does further initialization. If used outside
    of the VLLMConfig, some fields will be left in an improper state.

    It contains PassConfig, which controls the custom
    fusion/transformation passes. The rest has three parts:

    - Top-level Compilation control:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.mode|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.debug_dump_path|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cache_dir|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.backend|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.custom_ops|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.splitting_ops|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_mm_encoder|
    - CudaGraph capture:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mode|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_capture_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_num_of_warmups|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_copy_inputs|
    - Inductor compilation:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_sizes|
      - [`compile_ranges_endpoints`]
        [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_ranges_endpoints]
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_compile_config|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_passes|
      - custom inductor passes

    Why we have different sizes for cudagraph and inductor: - cudagraph:
    a cudagraph captured for a specific size can only be used for the
    same size. We need to capture all the sizes we want to use. -
    inductor: a graph compiled by inductor for a general shape can be
    used for different sizes. Inductor can also compile for specific
    sizes, where it can have more information to optimize the graph with
    fully static shapes. However, we find the general shape compilation
    is sufficient for most cases. It might be beneficial to compile for
    certain small batchsizes, where inductor is good at optimizing.

    backend = '' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.backend*
        The backend for compilation. It needs to be a string:

        - "" (empty string): use the default backend ("inductor" on
          CUDA-alike platforms).
        - "eager"/"openxla"/...: use the specified backend registered in
          PyTorch.
        - "full.module.name": a qualified name which can be used to
          import the

        backend function. We use string to avoid serialization issues
        when using compilation in a distributed setting. When the
        compilation mode is 1 or 2, the backend is used for the
        compilation directly (it sees the whole graph). When the
        compilation mode is 3, the backend supports both whole graph and
        piecewise compilation, available backends include eager,
        inductor, and custom backends, the latter of which can be
        defined via `get_compile_backend`. Furthermore, compilation is
        only piecewise if splitting ops is set accordingly and
        use_inductor_graph_partition is off. Note that the default
        options for splitting ops are sufficient for piecewise
        compilation.

    compile_ranges_endpoints = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.compile_ranges_endpoints*
        Endpoints for Inductor compile ranges. The compile ranges are
        [1, endpoints[0]], [endpoints[0] + 1, endpoints[1]], ...,
        [endpoints[-1] + 1, max_num_batched_tokens]. Compile sizes are
        also used single element ranges, the range is represented as
        [compile_sizes[i], compile_sizes[i]].

        If a range overlaps with the compile size, graph for compile
        size will be prioritized, i.e. if we have a range [1, 8] and a
        compile size 4, graph for compile size 4 will be compiled and
        used instead of the graph for range [1, 8].

    compile_sizes = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.compile_sizes*
        Sizes to compile for inductor. In addition to integers, it also
        supports "cudagraph_capture_sizes" to specify the sizes for
        cudagraph capture.

    cudagraph_capture_sizes = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_capture_sizes*
        Sizes to capture cudagraph. - None (default): capture sizes are
        inferred from vllm config. - list[int]: capture sizes are
        specified as given.

        Deprecated with model runner V2, which takes
        `prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes` and

        captured graph.

    cudagraph_copy_inputs = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_copy_inputs*
        Whether to copy input tensors for cudagraph. If the caller can
        guarantee that the same input buffers are always used, it can
        set this to False. Otherwise, it should set this to True, and
        the compiler will copy the input to an internally managed
        buffer. Default is False. Note that this flag is only effective
        when cudagraph_mode is PIECEWISE.

    cudagraph_decoder_replay = True class-attribute

        DeepSeek-V4.1) in CUDA graphs of their own, and trim them in
        PIECEWISE graph steps. Requires breakable PIECEWISE graphs; off
        under LoRA, prompt embeddings and non-first PP ranks.

    cudagraph_mm_encoder = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mm_encoder*
        Enable CUDA graph capture for multimodal encoder (ViT). When
        enabled, captures full encoder forward as CUDA graph for each
        token budget level.

    cudagraph_mode = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mode*
        The mode of the cudagraph:
        - NONE, no cudagraph capture.
        - PIECEWISE.
        - FULL.
        - FULL_DECODE_ONLY.
        - FULL_AND_PIECEWISE. (v1 default)

        PIECEWISE mode build piecewise cudagraph only, keeping the
        cudagraph incompatible ops (i.e. some attention ops) outside the
        cudagraph for general flexibility.

        FULL mode: Capture full cudagraph for all batches. Can be good
        for small models or workloads with small prompts; not supported
        by many backends. Generally for performance FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
        is better.

        FULL_DECODE_ONLY mode: Capture full cudagraph for decode batches
        only. Mixed prefill-decode batches are run without cudagraphs.
        Can be good for decode instances in a P/D setup where prefill is
        not as important so we can save some memory.

        FULL_AND_PIECEWISE mode: Capture full cudagraph for decode
        batches and piecewise cudagraph for prefill and mixed
        prefill-decode batches. This is the most performant mode for
        most models and is the default.

        Currently, the cudagraph mode is only used for the v1 engine.
        Note that the cudagraph logic is generally orthogonal to the
        compilation logic. While piecewise cudagraphs require piecewise
        compilation (mode=VLLM_COMPILE and non-empty splitting_ops),
        full cudagraphs are supported with and without compilation.

        Warning: This flag is new and subject to change in addition more
        modes may be added.

    cudagraph_num_of_warmups = 0 class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_num_of_warmups*
        Number of warmup runs for cudagraph. It means the first several
        runs will be treated as warmup runs. Only after that, the
        execution will be recorded, and the recorded cudagraph will be
        used for subsequent runs.

    cudagraph_specialize_lora = True class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_specialize_lora*
        Whether to create separate cuda graphs for cases with and
        without active LoRA adapters. When set to False, the
        LoRA-enabled cuda graph will be used for all cases, incurring
        the overhead of running LoRA ops even when no adapters are
        active. Setting this to True will remove this overhead at the
        cost of increased startup time and slightly higher memory usage.
        When `enable_lora` is False, this option has no effect.

    custom_ops = field(default_factory=list) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.custom_ops*
        Fine-grained control over which custom ops to enable/disable.
        Use 'all' to enable all, 'none' to disable all. Also specify a
        list of custom op names to enable (prefixed with a '+'), or
        disable (prefixed with a '-'). Examples:
        - ['all', '-op1'] to enable all except op1
        - ['none', '+op1', '+op2'] to enable only op1 and op2

        By default, all custom ops are enabled when running without
        Inductor and disabled when running with Inductor:
        mode>CompilationMode.NONE and backend="inductor". Inductor
        generates (fused) Triton kernels for disabled custom ops.

    debug_dump_path = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.debug_dump_path*
        The path to dump the debug information.

    decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes*
        Request counts of the FULL CUDA graphs for uniform decode
        batches, whose requests all have the same query length `q`:
        `1 + num_speculative_tokens` for the target model, K or K + 1
        for DSpark, DFlash and multi-module MTP drafters. A runner
        captures `n` requests as `n * q` tokens, for each `n` up to the
        most requests its batches have and the recorded
        `max_cudagraph_capture_size // q`. One-token draft decodes
        (EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP) take the request-count grid up to
        `max_num_seqs` instead. `[]` captures none. None (default): the
        request-count grid up to
        `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests`.

        With adaptive verification, the target model's decode batches
        mix query lengths, so they take token-keyed FULL graphs instead:
        the token-count grid up to
        `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)`
        tokens, within `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens`. These
        request counts then set the draft decode graphs alone.

    decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes = field(default_factory=list)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes*
        Decoder replay CUDA graph sizes for YOCO models (e.g.
        DeepSeek-V4.1), at most max_num_batched_tokens. If empty: the
        powers of two below sliding_window, then multiples of
        sliding_window up to min(max_cudagraph_capture_size,
        max_num_seqs * sliding_window), coarser past 16 *
        sliding_window. Larger replay batches run eagerly.

    decoder_replay_trim_threshold = Field(default=768, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.decoder_replay_trim_threshold*
        For YOCO models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1), PIECEWISE graphs with at
        least this many padded tokens trim the decoder replay batch;
        must exceed the replay window (128), below which nothing trims.
        Independent of the replay graph capture sizes; eager steps still
        trim.

    encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.encoder_cudagraph_max_frames_per_batch*
        Maximum total video frames per batch for encoder CUDA graph
        capture. Controls the cu_seqlens buffer size (one entry per
        attention sequence, i.e. one per video frame). If None
        (default), auto-inferred as
        encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch *
        max_frames_per_video (model-specific value according to
        processing_info). Positive value overrides auto-inference and
        applies to all budget levels. If we limit the video count per
        prompt to `0`, it will also be set to `0` (i.e., fall back to
        image-only mode).

    encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget = 5120 class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget*
        Largest auto-generated encoder CUDA graph token budget; must be
        positive or None. A batch with more tokens runs eagerly. The
        default balances graph memory against replay coverage;
        performance depends on the model, batch shape, and hardware.
        None captures up to the model's largest budget. Ignored when
        encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets is set.

    encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch = 0 class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch*
        Maximum number of images/videos per batch for encoder CUDA graph
        capture. Determines the fixed batch size used during graph
        capture. If 0 (default), auto-inferred as max_budget //
        min_budget from the model's budget range. User-provided positive
        value overrides auto-inference. A batch with more items runs
        eagerly in one forward.

    encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets = field(default_factory=list)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets*
        Token budget levels for encoder CUDA graph capture. Each budget
        defines a fixed token capacity. At runtime, a batch replays the
        smallest budget that holds it, or runs eagerly if none does. If
        empty (default), generated over the model's budget range:
        quarter-octave steps up to 1024 tokens, steps of 128 up to 2560,
        then 1/8-octave steps, up to
        `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget`. User-provided values
        override auto-inference. Example: [2048, 4096, 8192, 13824]

    fast_moe_cold_start = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.fast_moe_cold_start*
        Optimization for fast MOE cold start.

        This is a bit of a hack that assumes that: 1. the only decoder
        forward pass being run is the current model 2. the decoder
        forward pass runs all of the MOEs in the order in which they are
        initialized

        When the above two conditions hold, this option greatly
        decreases cold start time for MOE models.

        The options are: - True: optimization is always on - False:
        optimization is always off - None: optimization is on usually
        but off for speculative decoding

        If conditions 1&2 don't hold then this option will lead to
        silent incorrectness. The only condition in which this doesn't
        hold is speculative decoding, where there is a draft model that
        may have MOEs in them.

        NB: We're working on a longer-term solution that doesn't need
        these assumptions.

    max_cudagraph_capture_size = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size*
        The maximum cudagraph capture size.

        If cudagraph_capture_sizes is specified, this will be set to the
        largest size in that list (or checked for consistency if
        specified). If cudagraph_capture_sizes is not specified, the
        list of sizes is generated automatically following the pattern:

        >python
            [1, 2, 4] + list(range(8, 256, 8)) + list(
            range(256, max_cudagraph_capture_size + 1, 16))
<
        If not specified, max_cudagraph_capture_size is capped at 512 by
        default, or 1024 on data center Blackwell GPUs. This avoids OOM
        in tight memory scenarios with small max_num_seqs, and limits
        capture of large graphs that increase startup time and memory
        usage. Uniform decode sizes are appended only within this
        default ceiling.

        Deprecated with model runner V2, which takes
        `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens` (tokens) and
        `max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests` (requests) instead.
        After config resolution it holds the token count of the widest
        captured graph.

    max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests*
        Largest request count of a decode CUDA graph; with adaptive
        verification it also bounds the verify graphs' tokens (see
        `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes`). None (default):
        `max_num_seqs` on SM100 GPUs, otherwise the most requests that
        the platform's default `max_cudagraph_capture_size` holds at the
        target model's query lengths. Graphs no wider than the widest
        prefill graph mostly reuse its memory in the shared graph pool.
        Wider graphs, and FULL graphs of models with large per-token
        buffers (e.g. DeepSeek's indexer at a long `max_model_len`),
        take memory from the KV cache.

    max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens = Field(default=None, ge=1)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.max_decode_cudagraph_capture_tokens*
        Token budget of a uniform decode CUDA graph: each runner
        captures `n` requests at query length `q` only while `n * q`
        fits, and wider decode batches take the prefill graphs. It also
        bounds adaptive verification's token-keyed graphs. None
        (default): 8192 on SM100 GPUs, otherwise no budget. Wider decode
        graphs take memory from the KV cache.

    max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens*
        Largest token count of a prefill CUDA graph. None (default):
        8192 on SM100 GPUs, otherwise the platform's default
        `max_cudagraph_capture_size`; at most `max_num_batched_tokens`.
        More and wider graphs take memory from the KV cache and lengthen
        startup.

    mode = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.mode*
        The compilation approach used for torch.compile-based
        compilation of the model.

        - None: If None, we will select the default compilation mode.
          For V1 engine this is 3.
        - 0: NONE: No torch.compile compilation is applied, model runs
          in fully eager pytorch mode. The model runs as-is.
        - 1: STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE: The standard `torch.compile`
          compilation pipeline.
        - 2: DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE: Single Dynamo trace through the model,
          avoiding recompilation by removing guards. Requires no
          dynamic-shape-dependent control-flow.
        - 3: VLLM_COMPILE: Custom vLLM Inductor-based backend with
          caching, piecewise compilation, shape specialization, and
          custom passes.

    pass_config = field(default_factory=PassConfig) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.pass_config*
        Custom inductor passes, see PassConfig for more details

    prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes*
        Token counts of the CUDA graphs for prefill batches: every batch
        that is not a uniform decode batch, i.e. one with a prefill or
        with requests of different query lengths, and every batch when
        `cudagraph_mode` is FULL or PIECEWISE. Decode batches under
        adaptive verification are the exception; see
        `decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes`. `[]` captures none,
        and sizes above `max_num_batched_tokens` are dropped. None
        (default): the token-count grid up to
        `max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens`.

    splitting_ops = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.splitting_ops*
        A list of ops to exclude from cudagraphs, used in piecewise
        compilation.

        The behavior depends on use_inductor_graph_partition:
        - When use_inductor_graph_partition=False (default): These ops
          are used for Dynamo FX-level graph splitting. The graph is
          split at these ops before Inductor compilation, creating
          separate subgraphs for cudagraph capture.
        - When use_inductor_graph_partition=True: These ops are used to
          register Inductor partition rules. The graph partitioning
          happens at Inductor codegen time after all passes and fusions
          are finished, allowing compilation and custom passes to
          operate on the full graph while still excluding these ops from
          cudagraphs.

        If None, defaults to attention ops for piecewise cudagraphs. If
        empty list [], no ops are excluded (suitable for full
        cudagraphs).

    static_all_moe_layers = field(default_factory=list, init=False)

        The names of all the MOE layers in the model

    use_breakable_cudagraph = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.use_breakable_cudagraph*
        Whether to use breakable CUDA graphs (runtime stream-capture
        breaks instead of torch.compile FX graph splitting).

        Resolved by VllmConfig.post_init: an explicit
        VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH env var takes precedence, otherwise
        it is auto-enabled for breakable-by-default architectures (and
        for tuned batch-invariant setups). None means unresolved;
        readers fall back to envs.VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH so
        standalone CompilationConfig users keep working. Stored
        per-config (and pickled to workers) rather than written back to
        os.environ.

    use_inductor_graph_partition = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig.use_inductor_graph_partition*
        Use inductor graph partition to split the graph at
        cudagraph_unsafe ops. This partition happens at inductor codegen
        time after all passes and fusions are finished. It generates a
        single `call` function which wraps cudagraph-safe ops into
        partition functions and leave cudagraph-unsafe ops outside the
        partition functions. For a graph with N cudagraph-unsafe ops
        (e.g., Attention), there would be N+1 partitions. To mark an op
        as cudagraph unsafe, we can add
        `tags=(torch._C.Tag.cudagraph_unsafe)` when register the custom
        op.

        This config supports both full cudagraph and piecewise cudagraph
        without compiling twice. For piecewise cudagraph, it applies
        vLLM CUDAGraph wrapper to each partition. For N+1 partitions,
        there would be N+1 CUDAGraph wrapper instances.

        For full CUDAGraph, we always apply a single CUDAGraph wrapper
        outside the inductor `call` function in the model runner. The
        top-level full cudagraph capture ignores all partitioning.

    *vllm.config.compilation.CompilationConfig._skip_none_validation*

        delayed.

    evaluate_guards = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.DynamicShapesConfig.evaluate_guards*
        A debug mode to detect and fail if Dynamo ever specializes a
        dynamic shape by guarding on it. When True, dynamic shape guards
        are not dropped from dynamo. And a failure will be triggered if
        a recompilation ever happens due to that. This mode requires
        VLLM_USE_BYTECODE_HOOK to be 0. Enabling this allow observing
        the dynamic shapes guards in the tlparse artifacts also. When
        type is backed, aot_compile must be disabled for this mode to
        work. until this change picked up
        https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/169239.

    type = DynamicShapesType.BACKED class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.compilation.DynamicShapesConfig.type*
        Controls the type of dynamic shapes handling to use with
        torch.compile().

        - BACKED: Default PyTorch behavior with potential guards
          ignored.
        - UNBACKED: No guards guaranteed (most sound) but may throw data
          dependent errors.
        - BACKED_SIZE_OBLIVIOUS: Experimental safer alternative to
          backed/unbacked.

    compile_factors()
    *vllm.config.compilation.DynamicShapesConfig.compile_factors*

PassConfig
    Configuration for custom Inductor passes.

    This is separate from general `CompilationConfig` so that inductor
    passes don't all have access to full configuration - that would
    create a cycle as the `PassManager` is set as a property of config.

    You must pass PassConfig to VLLMConfig constructor via the
    CompilationConfig constructor. VLLMConfig's post_init does further
    initialization. If used outside of the VLLMConfig, some fields may
    be left in an improper state.

        fuse_act_padding (bool)

                       *vllm.config.compilation.decode_cudagraph_capture_grid*

decode_cudagraph_capture_grid(max_requests)
    The request-count grid up to `max_requests`: every count up to 6,
    then a step of the largest power of two not above 0.65 * n^(2/3) (2
    from 8, 4 from 16, 8 from 48, 16 from 128, 32 from 352): 64 sizes at
    1024.

                 *vllm.config.compilation.decode_cudagraph_capture_max_tokens*

decode_cudagraph_capture_max_tokens(config)
    The most tokens a uniform decode graph holds: the recorded max,
    which attention backends size their buffers by, within the decode
    token budget.

                     *vllm.config.compilation.decode_cudagraph_capture_shapes*

decode_cudagraph_capture_shapes(sizes, query_lens, max_tokens)
    The `(num_reqs, query_len)` uniform decode graphs for the request
    counts `sizes`, for each query length up to the most requests it
    maps to and `max_tokens` tokens. A batch pads to the smallest graph
    that holds it, so the first size above a limit is captured at the
    limit and larger ones are unreachable.

                      *vllm.config.compilation.prefill_cudagraph_capture_grid*

prefill_cudagraph_capture_grid(max_tokens, dense_head=False)
    The token-count grid up to `max_tokens`: 1, 2, 4, every 8 up to 64,
    four sizes per doubling up to 1024 (every count up to 32 with
    `dense_head`), then every 256 tokens, and every 512 once 7% of the
    size exceeds 512: 54 sizes at 8192.

                     *vllm.config.compilation.validate_cudagraph_capture_grid*

validate_cudagraph_capture_grid(sizes, limit)
    Normalize a platform grid, rejecting sizes outside its resolved
    limit.

                *vllm.config.compilation.varlen_decode_cudagraph_capture_grid*

varlen_decode_cudagraph_capture_grid(max_tokens, dense_head=False)
    The token-count grid of adaptive verification's decode graphs: 1, 2,
    4 (every count up to 32 with `dense_head`), then 4 sizes per
    doubling from 8 to 1024, every 128 up to 4096 and every 256 beyond.
    Adaptive verification picks its verify budget from the captured
    sizes, so it needs a finer grid than prefill.

            are

    cpu_offload = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.cpu_offload*
        Store embedding weights in pinned CPU memory for UVA lookup.

    disk_offload = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.disk_offload*
        Keep Qwen4Exp PLE tables in the checkpoint files and read each
        step's rows on the host instead of allocating the table. Takes
        precedence over cpu_offload.

    dp_shared_memory = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.dp_shared_memory*
        Share CPU-offloaded embedding weights between co-located DP
        replicas. Each node stores one copy of every TP shard, reducing
        host memory without per-step Engram DP collectives. Uses
        host-NUMA cuMem shared by FABRIC handle where supported (on
        ROCm, HIP VMM host memory with VLLM_ROCM_ENGRAM_HIP_VMM=1), else
        /dev/shm (which then needs capacity and a shared IPC namespace).
        Defaults to enabled when the model and other settings allow it;
        Flash uses private replicas. Falls back to per-replica tables
        when DP replicas are not co-located on one node or the host
        cannot hold them.

    embedding_across_dp = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.embedding_across_dp*
        Shard embeddings across TP and all DP ranks when enabled.
        Otherwise, each DP rank has a separate TP-sharded embedding
        replica.

    peer_group_fetch = 'sync' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_fetch*
        Where a peer group's fetch kernels run. `sync`: on the compute
        stream, started before the decoder layers, each Engram layer
        waiting for its own rows; over RDMA the rows move without SMs in
        between. `async`: on a side stream beside the layers, so their
        SM work (all of NVLink's gather) overlaps compute. Full CUDA
        graphs capture both; piecewise ones break at the start and at
        each Engram layer's wait.

    peer_group_rdma_inflight = Field(default=8, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_rdma_inflight*
        With `rdma`, the most prefill-sized gathers (64 WRs each) a
        GPU's NIC has in flight for its peers; 0 means no limit.
        Decode-sized fetches bypass it, so one engine's prefill delays
        another engine's decode by at most this backlog. The default (~2
        MB) keeps prefill fetches at full rate.

    peer_group_size = 0 class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_size*
        Split each table's rows over this many GPUs of several engines
        (the sum of their GPU counts); lookups read rows from the owning
        GPU. Every engine passes the same value, `peer_group_store` and
        `peer_group_transport`. Requires a model with Engram pool
        support (DeepSeek V4.1), CUDA, TP=1 and PP=1.

    peer_group_store = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_store*
        File through which a peer group's engines meet once at startup.
        Required with `peer_group_size`: the same path for every engine,
        reachable by all of them and fresh per launch (e.g. under a
        per-job directory).

    peer_group_thp_dir = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_thp_dir*
        With `rdma` and cpu_offload: a directory on a tmpfs mounted with
        `huge=always`, where host shards are placed on transparent huge
        pages. NICs gather rows at random, so a large shard on base
        pages misses the NIC's address-translation cache on nearly every
        row, which can make large fetches several times slower.

    peer_group_transport = 'nvlink' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.peer_group_transport*
        How a peer group reads rows: `nvlink` loads them from peers' HBM
        (CUDA FABRIC handles, an IMEX channel, cpu_offload=False); with
        `rdma`, the NICs of the GPUs holding them gather them from HBM,
        or from host memory with cpu_offload.

    use_thp = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.engram.EngramConfig.use_thp*
        Back private CPU-offloaded tables with transparent huge pages
        (best effort, falls back to ordinary pinned pages). Prefaulting
        the tables at startup takes longer. Requires cpu_offload without
        dp_shared_memory. Always on for private tables on ROCm.

    compile_factors()

                            *vllm.config.fault_tolerance.FaultToleranceConfig*

FaultToleranceConfig
    Configuration for fault tolerance.

    Attributes: ~
        engine_recovery_timeout_sec (int)
            Timeout (in seconds) to wait for error handling instructions

        request_failure_policy (Literal['recompute', 'fail'])
            Policy for handling unfinished requests when the engine encounters
            a fault.

    engine_recovery_timeout_sec = 120 class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.fault_tolerance.FaultToleranceConfig.engine_recovery_timeout_sec*
        Timeout (in seconds) to wait for error handling instructions
        before raising an exception. If the EngineCore encounters an
        error, it waits up to this many seconds for vLLM to receive
        instructions on how to handle the error and then recover from
        the fault. If vLLM does not recover during this time, the
        original error is raised.

    request_failure_policy = 'fail' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.fault_tolerance.FaultToleranceConfig.request_failure_policy*
        Policy for handling unfinished requests when the engine
        encounters a fault. 'recompute': preempt requests back to the
        waiting queue to recompute their KV cache and continue
        generation after recovery, without abort notifications. 'fail':
        abort unfinished requests immediately (default). Passing
        `params={"abort": true}` to the `retry` instruction discards
        queued requests even when the policy is 'recompute'.

                          *vllm.config.fault_tolerance.ft_tp_barrier_required*

ft_tp_barrier_required(parallel_config)
    Whether the per-step FT barrier over the TP cpu group is armed.

    The barrier makes TP peers fail on the host within the gloo timeout
    instead of leaving an orphaned TP collective on the device stream.

    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.backend_per_kind*
        Per-KV-cache-group attention backend overrides, keyed by
        `KVCacheSpecKind` (e.g.
        `{"mla_attention": "FLASHINFER_MLA", "sliding_window_mla": "TRITON_MLA"}`).

        kinds not listed fall back to `backend` (or automatic
        selection). A selected backend that is invalid for that kind
        raises at startup.

    hisparse_config = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.hisparse_config*
        HiSparse host-resident KV configuration. Setting this enables
        experimental Model Runner V2-only HiSparse DSA and QSA decode
        hot-buffering. It is inferred with defaults when
        HiSparseConnector is configured (directly or via
        MultiConnector); set it explicitly only to tune its fields.

    indexer_decode_cp = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.indexer_decode_cp*
        Split the sparse-attention indexer's decode scoring across the
        tensor-parallel ranks by context instead of by index head: each
        rank scores a 1/TP slice of the index-K pages for every head and
        the ranks exchange their local top-k, so each reads 1/TP of the
        index-K cache per sparse layer. The index-K cache stays
        replicated, so this is unrelated to
        `--decode-context-parallel-size`, which shards the KV cache
        itself; the two cannot be combined. Implemented for the MiniMax
        M3 NVFP4 indexer, which needs `indexer_kv_dtype="nvfp4"` and TP
        4 (one index head per rank); it is ignored with a warning where
        it does not apply. It pays off from about 4 concurrent decodes
        at 128K context and grows with batch and context.

    indexer_kv_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.indexer_kv_dtype*
        Data type for the sparse-attention indexer K cache. "auto" picks
        the model's default (bf16 for MiniMax M3, fp8 for the DeepSeek
        sparse indexer, mxfp4 for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm CDNA4 with aiter).
        Quantized formats (fp8, mxfp4, nvfp4) require indexer kernel
        support in the backend; MiniMax M3 supports nvfp4 on
        SM100/SM103/SM107 with at most 8 decode queries per request.

    indexer_logits_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.indexer_logits_dtype*
        Output dtype of DeepGEMM's dense MQA-logits kernels in the
        DeepSeek sparse-attention indexer. "auto" (default) picks the
        model's default: "bfloat16" for DeepSeek-V3.2 and DeepSeek-V4 on
        SM100, "float32" otherwise. "float32" reduces the head-weighted
        scores in FP32 and feeds them to the top-k as is. "bfloat16"
        halves the logits memory; on SM100 it also reduces in BF16 with
        BF16 head weights and lets the DeepSelect top-k rank the logits
        directly, while other top-k kernels read an FP32 copy. The
        sparse MQA-logits path (`indexer_sparse_logits`) emits BF16 on
        SM100 and FP32 on SM90 and ROCm, independently of this setting.

    indexer_sparse_logits = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits*
        Score only candidate blocks in the DeepSeek V4.1 two-level
        indexer. None (default) enables it on SM90 and supported SM100
        configurations; True forces it; False uses dense scoring.
        Requires no context parallelism. SM90 uses CuTe DSL with FP8
        cache and dense fallback for short prefills. Unsupported cache,
        model geometry or microbatching raises at initialization,
        including with the default None. SM100 requires DeepGEMM >= 2.8
        and DeepSelect (FP8/MXFP4 cache). ROCm gfx950 uses aiter with
        MXFP4 cache and remains opt-in.

    minimax_m3_indexer_cp = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_indexer_cp*
        MiniMax M3 on ROCm with tensor_parallel_size > 1: score the
        sparse indexer context-parallel at decode. Each rank reads 1/TP
        of the index cache, scores every index head on it, and per-head
        top-k candidates are exchanged and merged, so the selected
        blocks match the default path. `indexer_kv_dtype` picks the
        kernels that do it: a bf16 index cache ("auto" or "bf16") runs
        the Triton CP indexer, an fp8 e4m3 one the AITER MSA CP indexer
        on gfx950. This shards indexer work and not the KV cache, so it
        is not `decode_context_parallel_size` and requires that to be 1.

    minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend = 'cutlass' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend*
        Sparse decode kernel used by the MiniMax M3 MSA backend.
        "cutlass" falls back to Triton where the CUTLASS kernel does not
        support the platform, KV cache dtype, or head layout.

    mla_prefill_backend = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.mla_prefill_backend*
        MLA prefill backend to use. If None, will be selected
        automatically. Valid options: FLASH_ATTN (FA3/FA4), FLASHINFER,
        TRTLLM_RAGGED; on ROCm, ROCM_AITER_FA and ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8.
        ROCM_AITER_FLYDSL_FP8 is opt-in (gfx950, bf16 models): it
        quantizes Q/K/V to FP8 per tensor at runtime and falls back to
        ROCM_AITER_FA for inputs the FlyDSL kernel cannot take.

    sparse_mla_force_mqa = False class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_force_mqa*
        Force sparse MLA to use forward_mqa for all requests, including

        forward_mha when implemented. Set to True to always use the MQA

    sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor = Field(default=None, ge=2)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor*
        Sparse MLA prefill workspace size, in multiples of
        `max_model_len`. FlashMLA sparse gathers a prefill step's
        context KV into this workspace and runs attention in more chunks
        when the step holds more. The sparse indexer's prefill K buffer
        is sized to fit in the same memory. Lower values return memory
        to the KV cache at long `max_model_len`; the minimum of 2 leaves
        room for a full-length request's context-parallel shard. If
        None, 5 when `max_model_len` is at most 256K tokens, else 2.

    sparse_mla_shard_q = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_shard_q*
        Under tensor parallelism, shard sparse-MLA (DSA) prefill by
        token instead of by head: each TP rank runs the indexer and the
        sparse attention for its slice of the tokens with all heads, and
        all-to-all exchanges move the query and the attention output
        between the layouts. Applies to steps with at least
        `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` prefill tokens on the FlashInfer
        sparse MLA backend, or on FlashMLA sparse with an FP8 DeepSeek
        KV cache, without DCP, PCP or HiSparse. A mixed step's decode
        tokens stay sharded by head.

    sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens = Field(default=1024, ge=1)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.AttentionConfig.sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens*
        Minimum number of tokens after a step's decodes (requests of at
        most 1 + num_speculative_tokens tokens) for `sparse_mla_shard_q`
        to apply. Below it the all-to-all exchanges can cost more than
        they save.

    cache_dtype = 'auto' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.cache_dtype*
        Data type for kv cache storage. If "auto", will use model data
        type. An explicit float16 or bfloat16 must match the model data
        type. Custom dtypes can registered by platform backends via
        `register_kv_cache_dtype` are accepted (see vllm.config.cache).
        CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3) and fp8_e5m2. ROCm (AMD GPU)
        supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3). Intel Gaudi (HPU) supports fp8 (using
        fp8_inc). Some models (namely DeepSeekV3.2) default to fp8, set
        to bfloat16 to use bfloat16 instead, this is an invalid option
        for models that do not default to fp8. "nvfp4_4over6" uses the
        NVFP4 layout and selects between max/6 and max/4 scales per 16
        values by minimizing squared reconstruction error.

    enable_extensible_kv_cache = Field(default=None) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.enable_extensible_kv_cache*
        Reserve the KV cache address range with device virtual memory
        and commit physical pages after warmup, so the cache is sized
        from the memory actually free after CUDA graph capture rather
        than from a profiling estimate. If unspecified, enabled on CUDA
        and ROCm unless kv_cache_memory_bytes is set, or NIXL on device
        memory has no IMEX channel; falls back to estimate-based sizing
        where the driver lacks VMM support. Explicitly requesting it
        where unsupported is an error. On unpartitioned discrete ROCm
        GPUs, the sizing adds back free memory that HIP hides by
        counting each allocation as at least 2 MiB, so
        gpu_memory_utilization bounds exact device memory use there.
        When a KV connector registers the KV cache for RDMA or exports
        it to another process, each segment is backed by a single
        physical allocation; connectors declare this by overriding
        `KVConnectorBase_V1.kv_cache_access`.

    gpu_memory_utilization = Field(default=None, gt=0, le=1)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.gpu_memory_utilization*
        The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor,
        which can range from 0 to 1. For example, a value of 0.5 would
        imply 50% GPU memory utilization. This is a per-instance limit,
        and only applies to the current vLLM instance. It does not
        matter if you have another vLLM instance running on the same
        GPU. For example, if you have two vLLM instances running on the
        same GPU, you can set the GPU memory utilization to 0.5 for each
        instance. On non-GPU installs, this value controls the
        corresponding device memory utilization.

        If unspecified, 1.0 with the extensible KV cache (sized from
        measured memory) and 0.92 otherwise; see
        `resolved_gpu_memory_utilization`.

        With the extensible KV cache (the default on CUDA and ROCm),
        leave this unset unless something needs memory that vLLM does
        not measure: other processes sharing the GPU (including ones
        that allocate after vLLM has started), unified-memory devices
        whose memory the CPU also uses, weight transfer buffers for
        weight updates, or KV connectors that allocate their own device
        buffers. A lower value takes memory away from the KV cache.

    kv_cache_layout = field(default=None, init=False)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.kv_cache_layout*
        Resolved physical KV cache layout name (a `KVCacheLayout`
        member).

        `None` means the layout has not been resolved yet. The engine
        core resolves it once (`resolve_kv_cache_layout`) before memory
        profiling, and every worker process adopts the resolved name ---
        via the `set_kv_cache_layout` RPC, or
        `KVCacheConfig.kv_cache_layout` for workers spawned after
        resolution --- before the KV cache is allocated. Once set the
        value is final and read with `get_resolved_kv_cache_layout`,
        which raises on `None`. Tests and standalone tools may pre-set a
        value, which resolution then honors as-is.

    prefix_cache_retention_interval = Field(default=0, ge=0)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.prefix_cache_retention_interval*
        Token interval between retained sliding-window and Mamba
        prefix-cache checkpoints. `0` retains only semantic checkpoints,
        including the latest replay boundary and shared-prefix
        junctions. Positive values additionally retain periodic
        checkpoints at the specified interval, which must be a multiple
        of the scheduler block size. `None` retains checkpoints densely.
        Applies only to sliding-window and Mamba cache groups.

    prefix_caching_hash_algo = 'sha256' class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.prefix_caching_hash_algo*
        Set the hash algorithm for prefix caching:

        - "sha256" uses Pickle for object serialization before hashing.
          This is the current default, as SHA256 is the most secure
          choice to avoid potential hash collisions.
        - "sha256_cbor" provides a reproducible, cross-language
          compatible hash. It serializes objects using canonical CBOR
          and hashes them with SHA-256.
        - "xxhash" uses Pickle serialization with xxHash (128-bit) for
          faster, non-cryptographic hashing. Requires the optional
          `xxhash` package. IMPORTANT: Use of a hashing algorithm that
          is not considered cryptographically secure theoretically
          increases the risk of hash collisions, which can cause
          undefined behavior or even leak private information in
          multi-tenant environments. Even if collisions are still very
          unlikely, it is important to consider your security risk
          tolerance against the performance benefits before turning this
          on.
        - "xxhash_cbor" combines canonical CBOR serialization with
          xxHash for reproducible hashing. Requires the optional
          `xxhash` package.

    prefix_match_unit = Field(default=None, gt=0) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.prefix_match_unit*
        The finest token boundary (in tokens) a prefix-cache hit can
        land on.

        Prefix-cache keys are computed every `prefix_match_unit` tokens.
        It can be set finer than the physical KV cache block sizes (e.g.
        32 vs a 1024-token hybrid-model block) as long as every KV cache
        group's `block_size` is divisible by it, enabling cache hits at
        boundaries inside a physical block. It controls matching
        granularity only, not how often states are stored.

        This equals to the `hash_block_size` used throughout the KV
        cache code.

    replayssm_buffer_len = Field(default=16, gt=0) class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.replayssm_buffer_len*
        ReplaySSM logical history length B for Mamba2. Triton standard
        decode uses B physical rows; FlashInfer and Triton speculative
        decoding use B+T, where T is the target verification length.
        Kimi-K3 speculative decode does not use B. Default 16.

    resolved_gpu_memory_utilization property
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.resolved_gpu_memory_utilization*
        `gpu_memory_utilization`, or its default given the sizing mode.

    simple_cpu_offload_num_blocks = field(default=None, init=False)
    class-attribute instance-attribute

        Worker-aligned offload block count for
        `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.

    skip_page_size_padded = None class-attribute
    instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.skip_page_size_padded*
        Optional override for the page size of layers skipped from KV
        cache quantization (`--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers`); set during

    sliding_window = None class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.sliding_window*

    swa_bounded_replay = True class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.swa_bounded_replay*
        Keep the sliding-window KV of models that support it
        (DeepSeek-V4.1) out of prefix caching and rebuild it after a
        prefix hit by recomputing the hit's last window. The layers past
        the last KV-source layer then also run eager prefill steps on
        each request's trailing window only. Requires model runner V2.

    use_kda_recoverssm = field(default=False, init=False)
    class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.use_kda_recoverssm*
        Whether Kimi-K3 KDA uses RecoverSSM speculative decode.

    use_replayssm = False class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.use_replayssm*
        Use the ReplaySSM Mamba2 decode kernel: cache recent SSM inputs
        and skip the per-step full-state store, writing the checkpoint
        back only on flush. Triton and FlashInfer support Mamba prefix
        caching on and off. Mamba2 speculative decoding supports both
        backends. Pipeline parallelism is not supported. Flushes are
        most efficient when mamba_block_size is a multiple of
        replayssm_buffer_len, but this is not required.

    compile_factors()
    *vllm.config.CacheConfig.compile_factors*
        WARNING: Whenever a new field is added to this config, add it to
        `ignored_factors` if it does not affect the computation graph.

        Provide a hash that uniquely identifies all the configs that
        affect the structure of the computation graph from input
        ids/embeddings to the final hidden states, excluding anything
        before input ids/embeddings and after the final hidden states.

                                               *vllm.config.CompilationConfig*

CompilationConfig
    Configuration for compilation.

    You must pass CompilationConfig to VLLMConfig constructor.
    VLLMConfig's post_init does further initialization. If used outside
    of the VLLMConfig, some fields will be left in an improper state.

    It contains PassConfig, which controls the custom
    fusion/transformation passes. The rest has three parts:

    - Top-level Compilation control:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.mode|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.debug_dump_path|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cache_dir|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.backend|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.custom_ops|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.splitting_ops|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_mm_encoder|
    - CudaGraph capture:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mode|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_capture_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_prefill_cudagraph_capture_tokens|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_decode_cudagraph_capture_requests|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_num_of_warmups|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_copy_inputs|
    - Inductor compilation:
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_sizes|
      - [`compile_ranges_endpoints`]
        [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_ranges_endpoints]
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_compile_config|
      - |vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_passes|
      - custom inductor passes

    Why we have different sizes for cudagraph and inductor: - cudagraph:
    a cudagraph captured for a specific size can only be used for the
    same size. We need to capture all the sizes we want to use. -
    inductor: a graph compiled by inductor for a general shape can be
    used for different sizes. Inductor can also compile for specific
    sizes, where it can have more information to optimize the graph with
    fully static shapes. However, we find the general shape compilation
    is sufficient for most cases. It might be beneficial to compile for
    certain small batchsizes, where inductor is good at optimizing.

    backend = '' class-attribute instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CompilationConfig.backend*
        The backend for compilation. It needs to be a string:

        - "" (empty string): use the default backend ("inductor" on
          CUDA-alike platforms).
        - "eager"/"openxla"/...: use the specified backend registered in
          PyTorch.
        - "full.module.name": a qualified name which can be used to
          import the

        backend function. We use string to avoid serialization issues
        when using compilation in a distributed setting. When the
        compilation mode is 1 or 2, the backend is used for the
        compilation directly (it sees the whole graph). When the
        compilation mode is 3, the backend supports both whole graph and
        piecewise compilation, available backends include eager,
        inductor, and custom backends, the latter of which can be
        defined via `get_compile_backend`. Furthermore, compilation is
        only piecewise if splitting ops is set accordingly and
        use_inductor_graph_partition is off. Note that the default
        options for splitting ops are sufficient for piecewise
        compilation.

    *vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cache_dir*
        The directory to store the compiled graph, to accelerate
        Inductor compilation. By default, it will use model-related
        information to generate a cache directory.

        envs.VLLM_COMPILE_CACHE_SAVE_FORMAT) class-attribute
        instance-attribute
    *vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_cache_save_format*
        Format for saving torch compile cache:
        - "binary": saves as binary file (multiprocess safe)
        - "unpacked": saves as directory structure for
          inspection/debugging (NOT multiprocess safe)

        Defaults to `VLLM_COMPILE_CACHE_SAVE_FORMAT` if not specified.

    compile_mm_encoder = False class-attribute instance-attribute
