    requires_kv_delivery property
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.requires_kv_delivery*
        Whether this connector hands off KV that must be reliably
        delivered.

        If True, a request preempted while its hand-off is still pending
        is recomputed rather than allowed to finish and hand off blocks
        that the preemption already freed. Defaults to the producer
        role, since only a producer hands KV off when a request
        completes. Best-effort caches return False, as a dropped save is
        just a future cache miss.

    supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits property
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits*
        Whether external hits can complete divergent local hybrid hits.

        A capable connector restores lagging recurrent state when the
        local full-attention group reaches a deeper boundary. Defaults
        to False.

    get_block_ids_with_load_errors()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.get_block_ids_with_load_errors*
        Get the set of block IDs that failed to load.

        Returns: ~
            set[int]
                Set of block IDs that encountered load errors.

            set[int]
                Empty set if no load errors occurred.

          Notes: ~

          - Applies to both sync- and async-loading requests.
          - Async loading: failed blocks may be reported in any forward
            pass up to and including the pass where the request ID is
            returned by `get_transfer_results()`. Even if failures
            occur, the request must still be reported as finished
            receiving, and the failed block IDs must appear here no
            later than that same pass.
          - Sync loading: failed blocks should be reported in the
            forward pass in which they are detected.

    get_external_cache_hit_sources(request, num_external_tokens)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.get_external_cache_hit_sources*

        them.

        Called after `update_state_after_alloc`, so the load plan is
        known. Counts must sum to `num_external_tokens`; a mismatch is
        reported as `external_unspecified`. Only non-zero counts are
        included.

        Default: all tokens under `_cache_hit_source`.

    get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens)
    abstractmethod
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.get_num_new_matched_tokens*
        Get number of new tokens that can be loaded from the external KV
        cache beyond the num_computed_tokens.

        Parameters: ~
            request (Request)
                the request object.

            num_computed_tokens (int)
                the number of locally computed tokens for this request

        Returns: ~
            tuple[int | None, bool]
                A tuple with the following elements: - An optional
                number of tokens that can be loaded from the external KV
                cache beyond what is already computed. If None, it means
                that the connector needs more time to determine the
                number of matched tokens, and the scheduler should query
                for this request again later. - `True` if external KV
                cache tokens will be loaded asynchronously (between
                scheduler steps). Must be 'False' if the first element
                is 0.

          Notes: ~

          The connector should only consider the largest prefix of
          prompt- tokens for which KV cache is actually available at the
          time of the call. If the cache cannot be loaded for some
          tokens (e.g., due to connectivity issues or eviction), those
          tokens must not be taken into account.

    may_load_async(request)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.may_load_async*
        Whether `get_num_new_matched_tokens` may return
        `load_kv_async=True` for this request. With
        --max-num-inflight-kv-loads, such requests can start loading
        while the running batch is full.

        Called whenever the request enters the waiting queues, so must
        be cheap. A false positive holds back other async loads until a
        slot is free. Defaults to the P/D `do_remote_prefill` flag.

    on_kv_cache_ready()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.on_kv_cache_ready*
        Finish deferred registration after final KV sizing.

        Called on each worker before requests, after preceding device
        work. Normally follows warmup and capture. With
        VLLM_ELASTIC_EP_SCALE_UP_LAUNCH, it precedes deferred
        warmup/capture in warm_and_capture(). Must return in bounded
        time: an unbounded wait blocks engine startup. No hook timeout
        or cancellation is provided. Exceptions fail startup; background
        tasks are not awaited. Not called on sleep/wake.

    requires_piecewise_for_cudagraph(extra_config) classmethod
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.requires_piecewise_for_cudagraph*
        Check if this connector requires PIECEWISE CUDA graph mode.

        Connectors that use asynchronous layer-by-layer operations
        (wait_for_layer_load/save_kv_layer) should override this method
        to return True when those operations are enabled. These
        operations cannot be captured in CUDA graphs and will be skipped
        during replay, causing data races. PIECEWISE mode allows Python
        code to execute between graph pieces, ensuring proper
        synchronization.

        Parameters: ~
            extra_config (dict[str, Any])
                The kv_connector_extra_config dict from
                KVTransferConfig.

        Returns: ~
            bool
                True if this connector requires PIECEWISE CUDA graph
                mode,

            bool
                False otherwise.

    update_state_after_alloc(request, blocks, num_external_tokens)
    abstractmethod
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.update_state_after_alloc*
        Update KVConnector state after block allocation.

        If get_num_new_matched_tokens previously returned True for a
        request, this function may be called twice for that same request
        - first when blocks are allocated for the connector tokens to be
        asynchronously loaded into, and second when any additional
        blocks are allocated, after the load/transfer is complete.

        Decide whether to load based on `num_external_tokens`, not on
        whether `blocks` is empty: `blocks` may be non-empty even when
        `num_external_tokens == 0` (e.g. a non-chosen sub-connector of
        MultiConnector still receives the request's real blocks).

        Parameters: ~
            request (Request)
                the request object.

            blocks (KVCacheBlocks)
                the blocks allocated for the request.

            num_external_tokens (int)
                the number of tokens to load from the external KV cache.
                0 means nothing should be loaded.

    wait_for_save() abstractmethod
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base.KVConnectorBase_V1.wait_for_save*
        Submit saves and perform required synchronization.

        Called once per step, including empty steps, after any target
        and draft forwards. Metadata remains bound during this call. Do
        nothing if there is no save work.

        Async saves must retain their source blocks until completion is
        reported to the scheduler. Otherwise, wait for saves to finish
        before returning.

    _finish_previous_step()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.worker.HiSparseConnectorWorker._finish_previous_step*
        Mirror the previous step's draft-layer rows, then hand its pages
        over.

        Runs before this step's work, so after the previous step's
        drafter. Post-forward transfers are ordered behind the draft
        mirror, so a page is never reported clean, and its resident
        block never released, before its draft-layer rows reach the
        host. Both land in the previous step's host write event, which
        this step waits on before its forward and its host copies, since
        the scheduler may already have reused the finished requests'
        blocks they read and write.

    _resolve_row_mirrors(state)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.worker.HiSparseConnectorWorker._resolve_row_mirrors*
        Compute the final row mirrors from the staged GPU slot mapping.

    _restore_pages(transfers)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.worker.HiSparseConnectorWorker._restore_pages*
        Copy host pages into resident pages on every rank before its
        forward.

        Covers imported tails and promoted imports. One batched H2D call
        per step, instead of one copy per page and layer, keeps a long
        promoted import from flooding the stream with launches.

    _stage_row_mirror_mapping(num_tokens)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.worker.HiSparseConnectorWorker._stage_row_mirror_mapping*
        Snapshot the rows this forward will write, off the compute
        stream.

        The resident slot mapping is a persistent view bound at
        registration time, so the rows are already staged by the time
        the forward launches.

    invalidate_blocks(block_ids, request_state_indices)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hisparse.worker.HiSparseConnectorWorker.invalidate_blocks*
        Invalidate recycled host slots in this worker's leader runtimes.

    take_completed_host_copies()

        Drain host copies this worker has enqueued for this step.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
       *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.connector*

MooncakeStoreConnector - KV cache connector using
MooncakeDistributedStore.

Unlike MooncakeConnector which does direct P2P transfer, this connector
uses MooncakeDistributedStore as a shared KV cache pool. Both producer
and consumer instances read/write KV to/from the store independently,
enabling prefix caching via hash-based deduplication.

Classes: ~

MooncakeStoreConnector  KV connector using MooncakeDistributedStore as shared
                        KV pool.
MooncakeStoreKVEvents   KV event aggregation for MooncakeStoreConnector.

                          reset.

    get_mem_pool_context()

        Return a context manager for the custom MemPool, or None.

        Called by the Worker before `initialize_kv_cache` so that KV
        cache is allocated from the Mooncake-managed pool when
        `custom_mem_pool` is set in `kv_connector_extra_config`.

    reset_cache()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.connector.MooncakeStoreConnector.reset_cache*
        Reset the external Mooncake store on prefix-cache reset.

        Drains the worker send queue, then runs `remove_all` on the
        Mooncake master. Caller must first pause generation (e.g.
        `pause_generation`) so no new puts are enqueued during drain.

        Returns True on ack, False on failure, None for the worker role.

    shutdown()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.connector.MooncakeStoreConnector.shutdown*
        Release connector resources on teardown.

        Closes the worker's MooncakeDistributedStore handle. A
        TransferEngine the store created is released with that handle.
        An engine borrowed from MooncakeConnector stays owned by that
        connector. Invoked from the engine's explicit shutdown path and
        as a backstop from `__del__`; a no-op on the scheduler role,
        which holds no store handle.

        Process tokens and yield (start_idx, end_idx, block_hash)

        When there are fewer KV heads than TP ranks, chunks are

        assignment keys off the absolute `chunk_id` so a given chunk
        always lands on the same rank regardless of where the processed
        suffix begins.

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.layout.group_compact_kernel_blocks*

group_compact_kernel_blocks(cache, num_blocks)
    Group a layer cache to `num_blocks` manager blocks and report
    whether each manager block is one gapless byte run (moves as one
    region).

    Decided on the kernel-block view, before grouping: a manager block
    is a run of consecutive kernel blocks, so it is compact whenever
    each kernel block is. The grouped `cache[0]` alone cannot tell: tail
    padding in every kernel block makes it non-dense although no other
    block's data sits in the gaps.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
        *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.protocol*

Wire-format constants for the LookupKey ZMQ admin channel.

This is the single source of truth shared by `LookupKeyClient` and
`LookupKeyServer` on the scheduler<->worker rank-0 admin channel.

Wire format (REQ/REP over IPC):

>text
    Request: [msg_type: bytes] [payload_frames...]

      msg_type == LOOKUP_MSG:
          frame 1: num_tokens (u32 big-endian, 4 bytes); the worker derives
                   the aligned lookup length
          frame 2: hash_len (u16 big-endian, 2 bytes) — byte length of each
                   fixed-size block hash (0 when there are no hashes)
          frame 3: raw block hashes concatenated back-to-back (each hash_len
                   bytes); the server splits on hash_len
        Response: hit_length (u32 big-endian, first 4 bytes), followed by zero
                  or more 8-byte tail-key boundaries. Each entry is group_id
                  (u32), then boundary_tokens (u32).

      msg_type == RESET_MSG:
          (no payload frames)
        Response: [RESP_OK] or [RESP_ERR]
<
The first frame of every request is a named bytes tag (not a numeric
sentinel that aliases the data field) so the protocol stays
self-describing and extensible: adding new admin commands requires only
a new tag and a new dispatch branch.

Mirrors the named-tag convention used by the NIXL connector (see
`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/metadata.py`).

    _handle_boundary_state_offloads(offloads, meta)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler._handle_boundary_state_offloads*
        Attach exact boundary-state blocks to store jobs for this step.

        Flushed in the step they arrive: the CoW copy is enqueued before
        the connector event records, so this step's event fences the
        exact block. Entries ride the request's save meta when present,
        else an offload-only ReqMeta (`token_len_chunk=0` skips the
        normal save, `can_save=True` takes the normal enqueue and
        store-job pinning path).

    _reference_save_blocks(requests)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler._reference_save_blocks*
        Take a GPU block reference for every store job this step emits.

        The worker DMAs out of these blocks after the step that
        scheduled them, so a reference keeps them out of the free queue
        even once the request itself is freed, until every rank reports
        the job done.

    build_connector_meta(scheduler_output)

        Build connector metadata for this scheduler step.

        Check for external KV cache hit.

        Returns `(None, False)` when an async lookup is still in flight,
        signaling the scheduler to retry this request on a later step.

    has_pending_push_work()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler.has_pending_push_work*
        Keep the engine stepping while any store job still holds block
        refs.

        Completions only reach the scheduler as worker metadata on a
        step, so an engine that quiesced with jobs in flight would leave
        those references held indefinitely. Nothing else keeps it alive
        now that a finishing request no longer defers its own free.

    register_finished_lookahead_save(request, block_ids)

        update.

    register_finished_partial_tail(request, block_ids, partial_tail_offloads)

        Queue and pin a finish-time tail for the next connector step.

    reset_store()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler.reset_store*
        Trigger a global `remove_all(force=True)` on the Mooncake
        master.

        Routes through the existing LookupKey ZMQ admin channel to
        worker rank 0, which owns the `MooncakeDistributedStore` handle.

        Ordering assumption: caller (typically
        `Scheduler.reset_connector_cache`, invoked via
        `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`) MUST ensure no
        in-flight Mooncake lookups or transfers. For RL workflows this
        is satisfied at the step boundary after weight updates and
        rollout drain. Violating this can allow stale KV to be served on
        the next request, defeating the hard-reset guarantee.

        Returns True on ACK from worker, False on NACK or RPC error.

    start_lookup_prefetch(request)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler.start_lookup_prefetch*
        Start an async lookup as soon as the request is added, so it can
        complete while the request waits to be scheduled.

    update_connector_output(connector_output)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler.MooncakeStoreScheduler.update_connector_output*
        Drop the block references of store jobs every rank has finished.

    update_state_after_alloc(request, blocks, num_external_tokens)

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.scheduler._partial_tail_non_mamba_puts*

_partial_tail_non_mamba_puts(coord, req_meta, block_sizes)
    Locate the non-Mamba blocks a partial-tail save publishes.

    A later request resumes at the prompt's Mamba checkpoint
    (`boundary`) only if both pieces of KV are stored:

    - Mamba groups: the state at `boundary`, handed off by the core as a
      boundary put of its own, so Mamba groups are not listed here.
    - Other groups: the KV from the last LCM-aligned normal save up to
      `boundary`. Each block is keyed by the hash at its end, clipped to
      the checkpoint boundary.

    Groups whose KV is not computed yet are omitted. For example, with
    LCM 16, blocks of 4 tokens, and a checkpoint at 44, the
    full-attention blocks are 8-10, keyed at 36, 40 and 44.

    A Mamba state handed off at any other position, i.e. a shared-prefix
    junction (`--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`), adds no puts
    here.

    `block_sizes` are the per-group block sizes, indexed like
    `req_meta.block_ids`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease*

Selective read leases for Mooncake store prefix lookups.

`batch_is_exist` leases every key it finds, so a lookup renews every
stored key of the prompt, including keys a load of the hit skips, such
as blocks outside a sliding window or states at earlier block
boundaries. With `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE` the lookup probes
lease-free (`batch_probe_key`) and leases only the keys the hit will
load.

Classes: ~

SelectiveLookupLease  Leases only the keys a prefix-lookup hit will load.

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease.SelectiveLookupLease*

SelectiveLookupLease
    Leases only the keys a prefix-lookup hit will load.

    The lookup probes its candidates with `probe`, computes the hit as
    usual, and passes it through `lease_hit`.

    Methods: ~

    lease_hit    Lease the keys a load of `hit` reads and return the hit to
                 load.
    loaded_keys  Keys a load of `hit` reads, in every rank namespace, and
                 their
    probe        Existence of `keys`, without granting a lease.

    _lease(block_hashes, hit, load_masks)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease.SelectiveLookupLease._lease*
        Lease the keys a load of `hit` reads.

        Returns the `(group, hash)` pairs no longer in the store. Raises
        `_LeaseFailedError` when the lease RPC fails, including per-key
        error results.

    lease_hit(block_hashes, hit, load_masks, exists_set, longest_hit)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease.SelectiveLookupLease.lease_hit*
        Lease the keys a load of `hit` reads and return the hit to load.

        `exists_set` holds the probed `(group, hash)` pairs and
        `longest_hit` recomputes the hit from them. The lease covers
        only the keys this hit loads, e.g. the state at its tail
        boundary but not states at earlier boundaries. If a key was
        evicted since the probe, the shorter hit can end at one of those
        unleased keys, so it is leased in another round. Returns an
        empty hit if the lease fails or the hit keeps shrinking.

    loaded_keys(block_hashes, hit, load_masks)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease.SelectiveLookupLease.loaded_keys*
        Keys a load of `hit` reads, in every rank namespace, and their
        `(group, hash)` pairs.

        Mirrors `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread._handle_request`: each
        group's load mask (one entry per Store block), with the tail
        chunk keyed by the hit's tail boundary.

    probe(keys)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.selective_lease.SelectiveLookupLease.probe*
        Existence of `keys`, without granting a lease.

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.worker.LookupKeyServer*

LookupKeyServer
    ZMQ server on worker rank 0 for the LookupKey admin channel.

    Handles two request types, tagged at frame 0: - `LOOKUP_MSG`:
    prefix-cache hit query, returns its load plan. - `RESET_MSG`: drains
    the send thread queue, then runs `store.remove_all(force=True)`.
    Caller must have paused the scheduler first.

    close()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.worker.MooncakeStoreWorker.close*
        Release the MooncakeDistributedStore handle on teardown.

        Closing the store frees a TransferEngine it created, the RDMA
        buffers it registered, and the connection to the master server.
        An engine borrowed from MooncakeConnector stays owned by that
        connector; closing the store drops the store client's reference
        and unmounts the segments the store itself mounted. Idempotent
        so it is safe to call from both the explicit shutdown path and
        `__del__`.

    get_finished(finished_req_ids, meta)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.worker.MooncakeStoreWorker.get_finished*
        Get completed send/recv request IDs.

        wait_for_save().

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.worker._resolve_cache_prefix*

_resolve_cache_prefix(vllm_config)
    Return the configured cache_prefix, deriving one for "auto".

    "auto" namespaces keys by build and model identity, so a new image
    or model revision does not read KV written by a different
    deployment. Ranks and Store payload format are already part of the
    key.

*vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake_store.worker._split_disk_offload_load_batches*

_split_disk_offload_load_batches(keys, addrs, sizes, usable_budget_bytes,
    raw_budget_bytes)
    Split a GET into sub-batches that fit the owner's staging buffer.

    `addrs[i]` / `sizes[i]` are scatter-gather lists (K/V or multi-layer
    segments) for key `i`. `usable_budget_bytes` caps a multi-key batch;
    `raw_budget_bytes` is the hard per-key cap.

    Returns `(batches, oversize_key)`. Aborts with `([], key)` if any
    single key exceeds `raw_budget_bytes`; otherwise `oversize_key` is
    `None`.

    _prefill_backoff()
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_scheduler.NixlBaseConnectorScheduler._prefill_backoff*
        Trailing prompt tokens the prefiller must not compute; the
        decoder recomputes them locally.

        Mamba needs h(N-1) so the decoder can derive h(N) itself.
        DSV41's sliding window under bounded replay is not replayed
        after a P/D load, so it must be laid out for the token the
        decoder recomputes. Multi-module MTP needs to keep its whole
        lookahead window off of the prefiller, which would otherwise
        embed the unverified drafts in the MTP layer's KV cache. The
        decoder would never rebuild them, because the update is sized by
        the rejection count, which is zero for the first decode.

    _stop_heartbeat(req_id)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_scheduler.NixlBaseConnectorScheduler._stop_heartbeat*
        Remove req_id from heartbeat tracking (if tracked).

    _truncate_request_for_prefill(request)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_scheduler.NixlBaseConnectorScheduler._truncate_request_for_prefill*
        P-side only: drop the trailing `_prefill_backoff()` prompt
        tokens so the prefiller stops short of what the decoder
        recomputes locally. For Mamba that is the single token needed to
        yield h(N-1); for multi-module MTP it is the drafter's whole
        lookahead window.

        Guarded by `_p_side_truncated` to avoid repeated truncation if
        the request is preempted and rescheduled.

    get_exchange_clipped_blocks(block_ids, clip_ssm=True)
    *vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.nixl.base_scheduler.NixlBaseConnectorScheduler.get_exchange_clipped_blocks*
        Clip a request's block lists down to the transferable blocks.

        Sliding-window groups keep only the in-window tail: the KV cache
        manager allocates blocks for the entire sequence length and
        cleans up out-of-window blocks only prior to the
        `request_finished_all_groups` hook.

        SSM groups keep only their state-bearing slot: the trailing
        speculative scratch slots and everything before the running
        state (null placeholders and the previous step's superseded
        state) go.

        Use this at every block-id exchange point. Pass `clip_ssm=False`
        for per-step partial lists (host-buffer save), where the SSM
        strip does not apply.
